titel: In a Wooden Boat at Sea
text: You lie in an open wooden sailing boat, a good six metres long – at the stern on cushions, your head propped up against the aft thwart, feet towards the bow, safely below the gunwale. Gulls circle and dart over you, waves all around, water knocks hollow against the planks, the boat creaks, and now and then the wind catches the slack sail.

gruppen.name: see_fern
gruppen.text: Surf and swell far out, all around the horizon. It reaches you over the gunwale and is softened by it.

gruppen.name: wind
gruppen.text: A light wind that slowly rises and falls; in the gusts it freshens – the same gusts that fill the sail.

gruppen.name: wellen
gruppen.text: Single wave crests 7 to 32 m away, each in a different place, drifting with the wind. When one breaks with real force, there is a deep rumble.

gruppen.name: rumpf
gruppen.text: Slaps and splashes against the planks – on whichever side is dipping as the boat rolls. The wood resonates hollowly and carries every knock right to your ear; hard hits make the whole hull boom, and now and then a little spray flies over the gunwale and patters onto the wood beside you.

gruppen.name: knarzen
gruppen.text: Rowlocks, thwarts and frames work as the boat heels or a wave hits the hull: a calm, warm creaking that stays fixed to the boat – only the deep, woody creaks, no bright squeaks.

gruppen.name: segel
gruppen.text: The sail hangs slack on the mast in front of you, beyond your feet. In a gust it catches the wind: real cloth flutter swells, the canvas fills with a soft thump and collapses again.

gruppen.name: moewen_fern
gruppen.text: The distant chatter of the colony, from the same direction.

gruppen.name: moewen
gruppen.text: Five gulls keep to windward of the boat, ahead and to the left, circling in the wind and calling; now and then another answers. When the wind freshens or a wave breaks on the rock, they take fright.

gruppen.name: ueberflug
gruppen.text: About every half minute a gull shoots over the boat 3 to 5 m up – mostly with the wind, from front left to back right, sometimes against it. One call lands right overhead, its pitch dropping as it passes (Doppler); wingbeats as it approaches.

gruppen.name: moewen_weit
gruppen.text: A gull colony on a distant rock ahead and to the right, 150 to 370 metres away – its calls always come from that direction.

gruppen.name: felsen
gruppen.text: A rock juts out of the water about 20 m away. Now and then a wave slams into it – a hard impact, then the spray falls back. The boat slowly swings, so the rock wanders around you.

gruppen.name: zug
gruppen.text: Twice in ten minutes a flock of eight to twelve gulls passes 60 to 90 m away – for half a minute you hear it approach, go by calling and fade away: first with the rising wind, later back again.

gruppen.name: gaense
gruppen.text: Twice, high and far out, a skein of geese crosses the water – their calls carry for a long time, slowly pass and fade; later the skein comes back.

drehbuch: Calm sea; the gulls circle at ease.
Far out, a skein of geese passes; you can hear their calls for a long time.
A flock of gulls passes with the rising wind.
The wind freshens; the sail fills more often.
The waves grow, the hull is hit harder; the gulls call more excitedly, their cries blown about by the wind.
Heavy sea: breakers crash against the rock one after another.
The wind drops and the sea settles.
Calm again – the gulls circle lazily once more.
